name: Śrīnātha Cakravartī (Ācārya)
add: Nandgram Dham: the 49th branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.107); disciple of Advaita Ācārya; his notable disciple was Kavi Karṇapūra (Paramānanda Sena), son of Śivānanda Sena. A guru-praṇāma verse of Kavi Karṇapūra says only that he was born in a brāhmaṇa family. He installed Śrī Kṛṣṇa-rāya at Kāñcaḍāpāḍā near Kumārahaṭṭa. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śrīnivāsa Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: Maṇi-mañjarī, assisting Guṇa-mañjarī (Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī). Works: Ṣaḍ-gosvāmy-aṣṭaka and a commentary on the four core verses of the Bhāgavatam. The year of his birth is given as about 1517 or 1530 (disputed); the place and year of his disappearance are not recorded by tradition.

name: Subhananda Dvija
add: Nandgram Dham: «Dvija» marks him as a brāhmaṇa by birth; a kīrtana singer in Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura's group at the Ratha-yātrā in Purī (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 13.39, 13.110). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śuklāmbara Brahmacārī
add: Nandgram Dham: a poor brahmacārī of Navadvīpa who begged rice from door to door, offered it and ate the remnants; an early, close companion of the Lord (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.38, 17.20).

name: Śrī Śyāmānanda Prabhu
add: Nandgram Dham: born Duḥkhī (Dukhiyā), later Kṛṣṇadāsa; Dhāreṇḍā Bāhādurpur is near today's Kalaikunda (Midnapore). Works: Vṛndāvana-parikramā, Upāsanā-sāra-saṅgraha and poems in the Aprakāśita Pada-ratnāvalī. Nandgram Dham: the year and place of his disappearance are both disputed.

name: Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī
add: Nandgram Dham: her father Nṛsiṁha Bhāḍuḍī was of a respected family of Nadia. Her son Acyutānanda became a noted devotee.

name: Śrīdhara Svāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: his Bhāvārtha-dīpikā is the first complete commentary on the Bhāgavatam. Probably born in a village near Remuṇā (Balasore, Odisha); other ideas point to Gujarat, South India or Vārāṇasī. His guru Paramānanda Purī is named in the opening invocation of the Bhāvārtha-dīpikā. Abbot (mahant) of the Govardhana Maṭha at Purī; Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī and Śrīla Prabhupāda identify him as a tridaṇḍi-sannyāsī of the Viṣṇusvāmī (Rudra) sampradāya.

name: Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda
add: Nandgram Dham: born Abhay Charan De on 1 September 1896 in Calcutta; his father Gour Mohan De was a cloth merchant. The family was related to the wealthy Mullik merchants; his childhood home on Harrison Road faced the Mulliks' Rādhā-Govinda temple.

name: Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the bhakta-tattva of the Pañca-tattva; Nārada Muni (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 90). Nandgram Dham names his brothers Śrīpati, Śrīrāma and Śrīkānta. His courtyard, Śrīvāsa Aṅgana, is still shown at Māyāpura.

name: Subuddhi Rāya
add: Nandgram Dham: a big landholder and adhikārī in Gauḍa under the Sultanate, known to Sanātana Gosvāmī before either renounced. Made to lose caste, he met the Lord at Vārāṇasī, who told him simply to chant (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 25). He hosted Rūpa Gosvāmī for a month in Vṛndāvana, and lived in real poverty near Mathurā, selling firewood and feeding visiting Vaiṣṇavas.

name: Sulocana
add: Nandgram Dham: the forty-second branch of the Caitanya tree, named beside Cirañjīva (the forty-first), his fellow devotee of Śrīkhaṇḍa (Ādi 10.78–79); the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā places him at Śrīhaṭṭa instead. In Kṛṣṇa-līlā the gopī Candraśekharā, one of Śrī Rādhā's maidservants.

name: Sundarānanda Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: Maheśapura is on the Vetravatī river; a naiṣṭhika-brahmacārī, without children. His disappearance is on the full moon of Māgha (Anubhāṣya) or of Kārtika (another account).

name: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: his father's village Bhiṭādiyā is on the Brahmaputra in East Bengal. He kept a private Sanskrit diary (kaḍacā) of the Lord's years in Purī, and compiled a treatise on music, the Saṅgīta-dāmodara. Nandgram Dham gives his identity as Viśākhā, who taught Rādhā the arts; some call him Lalitā.

name: Tapana Miśra
add: Nandgram Dham: in Vārāṇasī his close associate was Candraśekhara, the physician of Kāśī (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 17, 19, 25). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Uddhāraṇa Datta Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: called Divākara Datta before he met Nityānanda (some accounts); the eleventh of the twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 129).

name: Uddhava dāsa (of Gadādhara's branch)
add: Nandgram Dham: he met Śrīnivāsa and Rāghava Gosvāmī at Sanātana Gosvāmī's hut at Nandīśvara; praised in a single verse of Yadunātha dāsa's Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta (35). His disappearance is not recorded.

name: Śrī Vakreśvara Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the fifth branch of the Lord's tree (Ādi 10.17); his seventy-two hours of dancing were twenty-four prahara without stopping. His dīkṣā guru is not recorded. His foremost disciple was Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī; he established Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kānta at Kāśī Miśra's house (the Gambhīrā).
